confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches of cost-of-living aggregators (Numbeo, Expatistan, livingcost.net) for 2026. I converted NZD to USD at about 0.59 USD per NZD. That rate is my estimate for mid-2026 from general knowledge and the relationship to AUD/USD. I did not search for a USD/NZD rate, so the conversion carries roughly ±3-5% uncertainty. Typical NZD prices used: cappuccino about 6.0 (range 4.80-7.50), domestic draft pint about 13 (range 8-16), inexpensive meal about 24.50, mid-range three-course meal for two about 110-118. The cocktail anchor (about NZ$18-20) relies mainly on a thin Expatistan sample of 8 data points and its relationship to beer prices, so it is less certain. The wine anchor (about NZ$13-14) comes from a small number of venue menus that may be out of date, combined with its relationship to beer prices, so it is also less certain. All four accommodation anchors are my own overall estimates for the July winter off-peak season, based on general knowledge. I did not search for or check any booking pages or listings, so these are the least certain anchors. The FX observation comes from the RBA exchange-rates page shown in search results: 0.6720 USD per AUD at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026. This is the latest RBA observation available on the generation date, not a rate from the July 2026 pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: Wellington is a compact, high-cost capital. Its food and drink prices are close to Auckland's, and its hospitality prices are roughly comparable to mid-sized Australian cities such as Canberra or Hobart. For accommodation, I assumed off-peak July rates a little below Auckland's.
